0.7148,0.1953,0.1094}{{e}}}}_{\mathit{i}}}}}\quad\textsc{right=\scriptsize{D-con}}

Figure 11
.
{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}\boldsymbol{F}_{\textbf{{D}}}}
dictionary typing

Figure
11
shows the typing rules for
dictionaries. The relation

\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Sigma}}}}};\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Gamma_{C}}}}}};\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Gamma}}}}}\vdash_{d}\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{d}}}}}:\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{Q}}}}}
denotes that dictionary
{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{d}}}
of
dictionary type
{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{Q}}}
is well-formed
under environments
{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Sigma}}}
,
{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Gamma_{C}}}}
and
{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Gamma}}}
.
Similarly to regular term variables
{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{x}}}
(
iTm-var
),
the type of a dictionary variable
{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\delta}}}
(
D-var
) is obtained
from the typing environment
{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Gamma}}}
.
The type of a dictionary constructor
{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{D}}}
(
D-con
), on the other
hand, is obtained by finding the corresponding entry in the method environment
{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Sigma}}}
and
substituting any types
\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\overline{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\sigma}}}_{\mathit{j}}}}
applied to it in the
corresponding class constraint
\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\mathit{TC}}}}\,{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\sigma}}}_{\mathit{q}}}}
. All
applied dictionaries
\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\overline{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{d}}}}_{\mathit{i}}}}
have to be well-typed with the corresponding
constraint. Finally, the corresponding method implementation has to be
well-typed in the reduced method environment
\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Sigma}}}_{{\mathrm{1}}}}}
, which only contains
the instances declared before
{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{D}}}
. As mentioned in
Section
3
, this reduced environment disallows
recursive method implementations, as this would significantly clutter the
coherence proof while, as a feature, recursion is completely orthogonal to the desired property.

Non-Overlapping Instances.

The main requirement for achieving coherence of type class resolution, is that
type class instances do not overlap. This requirement is common in Haskell and
is for example enforced in GHC (though strongly discouraged,
the
OverlappingInstances
pragma disables it).
By storing all method implementations (with their corresponding instances) in a
single environment
{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Sigma}}}
, this invariant can easily be made explicit.

Figure
10
shows the
environment well-formedness condition
\vdash_{ctx}\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Sigma}}}}};\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Gamma_{C}}}}}};\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Gamma}}}}}
for the method environment.
Besides stating well-scopedness, it denotes that the method
environment
{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Sigma}}}
cannot contain a second instance, for which the head of
the constraint overlaps with
\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\mathit{TC}}}}\,{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\sigma}}}}}
, up to renaming.
This key property will be exploited in our coherence proof.

Operational Semantics.

As
{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}\boldsymbol{F}_{\textbf{{D}}}}
is an extension of System F, its call-by-name operational
semantics are mostly standard. The non-standard rules can be found
in Figure
9
(bottom right), where
\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Sigma}}}}}\vdash\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{e}}}}}\longrightarrow\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{e}}}^{\prime}}}
denotes
expression
{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{e}}}
evaluating to
\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{e}}}^{\prime}}}
in a single step, under method
environment
{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Sigma}}}
.

The evaluation rules for dictionary application (
iEval-DApp
and

iEval-DAppAbs
) are identical to those for term and type application.
More interesting, however, is the evaluation for methods (
iEval-method
).
A method name applied to a dictionary evaluates in one step to the method
implementation, as stored in the environment
{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Sigma}}}
.

Metatheory.

{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}\boldsymbol{F}_{\textbf{{D}}}}
is type safe. That is, the
common progress and preservation properties hold:

Theorem 1 (Progress).

If
\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Sigma}}}}};\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\bullet}};\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\bullet}}\vdash_{tm}\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{e}}}}}:\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\sigma}}}}}
,
then either
{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{e}}}
is a value,
or there exists
\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{e}}}^{\prime}}}
such that
\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Sigma}}}}}\vdash\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{e}}}}}\longrightarrow\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{e}}}^{\prime}}}
.

Theorem 2 (Preservation).

If
\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Sigma}}}}};\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Gamma_{C}}}}}};\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Gamma}}}}}\vdash_{tm}\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{e}}}}}:\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\sigma}}}}}
,
and
\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Sigma}}}}}\vdash\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{e}}}}}\longrightarrow\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{e}}}^{\prime}}}
,
then
\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Sigma}}}}};\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Gamma_{C}}}}}};\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Gamma}}}}}\vdash_{tm}\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{e}}}^{\prime}}}:\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\sigma}}}}}
.

Analogously to
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.7227}\boldsymbol{\lambda}_{\textbf{{TC}}}}
,
{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}\boldsymbol{F}_{\textbf{{D}}}}

rejects recursive expressions (including mutual recursion and recursive
methods). This allows for a normalizing language, that is,
any well-typed expression evaluates to a value, after a finite number of steps.
Note that since the small step operational semantics are deterministic,
normalization implies strong normalization.

Theorem 3 (Strong Normalization).

If
\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Sigma}}}}};\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Gamma_{C}}}}}};\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\bullet}}\vdash_{tm}\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{e}}}}}:\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\sigma}}}}}

then all possible evaluation derivations for
{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{e}}}
terminate :

\exists{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{v}}}:\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Sigma}}}}}\vdash\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{e}}}}}\longrightarrow^{*}\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{v}}}}}
.

The proof follows the familiar structure for proving normalization using logical
relations, as presented by Ahmed
(
Ahmed 2015
)
, and can be found in
Section
K.4
of the appendix.

6.1.
Elaboration from
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.7227}\boldsymbol{\lambda}_{\textbf{{TC}}}}
to
{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}\boldsymbol{F}_{\textbf{{D}}}}

The green aspects in Figure
12
denote the elaboration of

{\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.7227}\boldsymbol{\lambda}_{\textbf{{TC}}}}
terms to
{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}\boldsymbol{F}_{\textbf{{D}}}}
. Similarly to the elaboration from
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.7227}\boldsymbol{\lambda}_{\textbf{{TC}}}}
to

{\color[rgb]{0.7148,0.1953,0.1094}\boldsymbol{F}_{\textbf{\lx@text@lbrace\lx@text@rbrace}}}
, we have adopted the convention
that any green
{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}\boldsymbol{F}_{\textbf{{D}}}}
types or constraints are the elaborated forms of their
identically named blue
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.7227}\boldsymbol{\lambda}_{\textbf{{TC}}}}
counterparts.
This elaboration works analogously to the elaboration from
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.7227}\boldsymbol{\lambda}_{\textbf{{TC}}}}
to
{\color[rgb]{0.7148,0.1953,0.1094}\boldsymbol{F}_{\textbf{\lx@text@lbrace\lx@text@rbrace}}}
,
as shown in Figure
3
.
The full set of rules can be found in Section
C.2
of the appendix.

The only notable case is
sTm-check-meth
, where the entailment relation
for solving the type class constraint
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.7227}{{\mathit{TC}}}}\,{\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.7227}{{\tau}}}
now results in a
dictionary
{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{d}}}
. As explained at the start of Section
6
,
unlike
{\color[rgb]{0.7148,0.1953,0.1094}\boldsymbol{F}_{\textbf{\lx@text@lbrace\lx@text@rbrace}}}
,

{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}\boldsymbol{F}_{\textbf{{D}}}}
differentiates syntactically between dictionaries and normal
expressions.

\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.7227}{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.7227}{{P}}}}};\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.7227}{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.7227}{{\Gamma_{C}}}}}};\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.7227}{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.7227}{{\Gamma}}}}}\vdash_{tm}^{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{M}}}\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.7227}{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.7227}{{e}}}}}\Leftarrow\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.7227}{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.7227}{{\tau}}}}}{\rightsquigarrow\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{e}}}}}}

Figure 13
.
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.7227}\boldsymbol{\lambda}_{\textbf{{TC}}}}
constraint entailment with elaboration to
{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}\boldsymbol{F}_{\textbf{{D}}}}

Type class resolution (Figure
13
) of a
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.7227}\boldsymbol{\lambda}_{\textbf{{TC}}}}

constraint
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.7227}{{Q}}}
results in a
{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}\boldsymbol{F}_{\textbf{{D}}}}
dictionary
{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{d}}}
.
When using a locally available constraint to resolve the wanted constraint
(
sEntail-local
), the corresponding dictionary variable
{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\delta}}}
is returned.
On the other hand, when resolving using a global instance declaration (
sEntail-inst
), a
dictionary is constructed by taking the corresponding constructor

{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{D}}}
and applying

(a)

the types
\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\overline{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\sigma}}}_{\mathit{j}}}}
needed for matching the wanted constraint to the instance
declaration and

(b)

the dictionaries
\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\overline{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{d}}}}_{\mathit{i}}}}
, constructed by resolving the
instance context constraints.

Metatheory.

We discuss the coherence of the elaboration from
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.7227}\boldsymbol{\lambda}_{\textbf{{TC}}}}
to
{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}\boldsymbol{F}_{\textbf{{D}}}}
in detail
in Section
7
, and mention here
that it is type preserving:

Theorem 4 (Typing Preservation - Expressions).

If
\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.7227}{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.7227}{{P}}}}};\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.7227}{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.7227}{{\Gamma_{C}}}}}};\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.7227}{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.7227}{{\Gamma}}}}}\vdash_{tm}^{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{M}}}\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.7227}{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.7227}{{e}}}}}\Rightarrow\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.7227}{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.7227}{{\tau}}}}}{\rightsquigarrow\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{e}}}}}}
,
and
\vdash_{ctx}^{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{M}}}\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.7227}{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.7227}{{P}}}}};\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.7227}{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.7227}{{\Gamma_{C}}}}}};\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.7227}{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.7227}{{\Gamma}}}}}\rightsquigarrow\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Sigma}}}}};\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Gamma_{C}}}}}};\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Gamma}}}}}
,
and
\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.7227}{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.7227}{{\Gamma_{C}}}}}};\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.7227}{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.7227}{{\Gamma}}}}}\vdash_{ty}^{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{M}}}\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.7227}{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.7227}{{\tau}}}}}\,{{\rightsquigarrow\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\sigma}}}}}}}
,

then
\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Sigma}}}}};\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Gamma_{C}}}}}};\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Gamma}}}}}\vdash_{tm}\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{e}}}}}:\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\sigma}}}}}
.

The same theorem holds for check mode, but is omitted for space
reasons. The full proofs can be found in Section
J.3
of the appendix.

Note that both the class environment
{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Gamma_{C}}}}
and the program context
{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Sigma}}}

are largely direct translations of their
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.7227}\boldsymbol{\lambda}_{\textbf{{TC}}}}
counterparts. One notable
difference is the fact that the environment
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.7227}{{\Gamma}}}
under which to interpret
the
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.7227}\boldsymbol{\lambda}_{\textbf{{TC}}}}

{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}\boldsymbol{F}_{\textbf{{D}}}}
method implementation.
Consider for instance the case of
\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{D}}}_{{\mathrm{2}}}}}
, where the variables

{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{a}}}

{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{b}}}
,
\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\delta}}}_{{\mathrm{1}}}}}
and
\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\delta}}}_{{\mathrm{2}}}}}
,
which in
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.7227}\boldsymbol{\lambda}_{\textbf{{TC}}}}
are implicitly provided by the typing environment, are now
explicit in the term level.

Elaborating the
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.7227}\boldsymbol{\lambda}_{\textbf{{TC}}}}
expression results in the following

\displaystyle\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\textbf{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{let}} }\,{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\mathit{refl}}}}:\forall{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{a}}}.{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{Eq}}}\,{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{a}}}\Rightarrow{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{a}}}\rightarrow\mathit{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{Bool}}}}}

\displaystyle\qquad\quad\,\,\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{=\Lambda{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{a}}}.\lambda{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\delta}}}_{{\mathrm{3}}}:{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{Eq}}}\,{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{a}}}.\lambda{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{x}}}:{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{a}}}.{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\delta}}}_{{\mathrm{3}}}.{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{(==)}}}\,{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{x}}}\,{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{x}}}\,}}

\displaystyle\qquad\quad\,\,\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{={\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\mathit{refl}}}}\,({\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{Int}}},{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{Int}}})\,({\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{D}}}_{{\mathrm{2}}}\,{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{Int}}}\,{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{Int}}}\,{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{D}}}_{{\mathrm{1}}}\,{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{D}}}_{{\mathrm{1}}})\,(5,42)\,}}

Unlike the corresponding
{\color[rgb]{0.7148,0.1953,0.1094}\boldsymbol{F}_{\textbf{\lx@text@lbrace\lx@text@rbrace}}}
expression, shown in Section
4.1
,
records storing the method types and implementations do not need to be passed
around explicitly.
In
{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}\boldsymbol{F}_{\textbf{{D}}}}

respectively. The construction of these dictionaries through type class
resolution is shown in Figure
13
.

2.2
, results in the following
{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}\boldsymbol{F}_{\textbf{{D}}}}
class environment
(since no instance declarations exist, the method environment
{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Sigma}}}
remains empty):

\displaystyle\qquad{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Gamma_{C}}}}=\penalty\

\displaystyle\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{base}}}:{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{Base}}}\,{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{a}}}:{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{a}}}\rightarrow\mathit{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{Bool}}}}}

\displaystyle\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{,}}\penalty\

\displaystyle\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{sub}}}_{{\mathrm{1}}}:{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{Sub}}}_{{\mathrm{1}}}\,{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{a}}}:{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{a}}}\rightarrow\mathit{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{Bool}}}}}

\displaystyle\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{,}}\penalty\

\displaystyle\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{sub}}}_{{\mathrm{2}}}:{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{Sub}}}_{{\mathrm{2}}}\,{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{a}}}:{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{a}}}\rightarrow\mathit{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{Bool}}}}}

The
{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}\boldsymbol{F}_{\textbf{{D}}}}
class environment no longer needs to
store superclasses, as these are all flattened into additional local
constraints during elaboration.

Similarly to Section
4.1
, we focus solely on elaborating

test2
, which results in the following
{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}\boldsymbol{F}_{\textbf{{D}}}}
expression:

\displaystyle\qquad\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\textbf{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{let}} }\,{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{test}}}_{{\mathrm{2}}}}}

\displaystyle\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{:\forall{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{a}}}.{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{Base}}}\,{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{a}}}\Rightarrow{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{Sub}}}_{{\mathrm{1}}}\,{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{a}}}\Rightarrow{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{Base}}}\,{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{a}}}\Rightarrow{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{Sub}}}_{{\mathrm{2}}}\,{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{a}}}\Rightarrow{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{a}}}\rightarrow\mathit{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{Bool}}}}}

\displaystyle\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{=\Lambda{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{a}}}.\lambda{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\delta}}}_{{\mathrm{1}}}:{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{Base}}}\,{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{a}}}.\lambda{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\delta}}}_{{\mathrm{2}}}:{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{Sub}}}_{{\mathrm{1}}}\,{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{a}}}.\lambda{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\delta}}}_{{\mathrm{3}}}:{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{Base}}}\,{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{a}}}.\lambda{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\delta}}}_{{\mathrm{4}}}:{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{Sub}}}_{{\mathrm{2}}}\,{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{a}}}.}}

\displaystyle\quad\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\lambda{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{x}}}:{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{a}}}.{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\delta}}}_{{\mathrm{1}}}.{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{base}}}\,{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{x}}}\,}}

\displaystyle\textbf{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{in}} }\,\mathit{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{True}}}\,\,

The only difference with the
{\color[rgb]{0.7148,0.1953,0.1094}\boldsymbol{F}_{\textbf{\lx@text@lbrace\lx@text@rbrace}}}
elaboration is that we now use class
constraints instead of passing around a record type (storing the method types).

6.2.
Elaboration from
{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}\boldsymbol{F}_{\textbf{{D}}}}
to
{\color[rgb]{0.7148,0.1953,0.1094}\boldsymbol{F}_{\textbf{\lx@text@lbrace\lx@text@rbrace}}}

As both
{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}\boldsymbol{F}_{\textbf{{D}}}}
and
{\color[rgb]{0.7148,0.1953,0.1094}\boldsymbol{F}_{\textbf{\lx@text@lbrace\lx@text@rbrace}}}
are extensions of System F, the elaboration
from former to latter is mostly trivial, leaving common features unchanged.
The mapping of
{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}\boldsymbol{F}_{\textbf{{D}}}}
dictionaries into
{\color[rgb]{0.7148,0.1953,0.1094}\boldsymbol{F}_{\textbf{\lx@text@lbrace\lx@text@rbrace}}}

records, however, is non-trivial.
Briefly, dictionary types are elaborated into record types, as shown in
Figure
9
(top right), and dictionaries into record expressions,
possibly nested within type and term abstractions and applications, as shown in
Figure
11
.

In particular, a dictionary type,
{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\mathit{TC}}}}
, which corresponds to a unique entry

(\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{m}}}:{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\mathit{TC}}}}\,{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{a}}}:{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\sigma}}}^{\prime}}})
in the class environment
{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Gamma_{C}}}}
, elaborates to a record
type whose field has the same name as the dictionary type’s method name,
{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{m}}}
, and the type of
that field is determined by the elaboration of
\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\sigma}}}^{\prime}}}
. A
{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\mathit{TC}}}}\,{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\sigma}}}
dictionary
elaborates to a record expression which is surrounded, firstly, by abstractions over
type and term variables that arise from the method type’s class constraints and, secondly,
by type and term applications that properly instantiate those abstractions.

Metatheory.

The following theorems confirm that the
{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}\boldsymbol{F}_{\textbf{{D}}}}
-to-
{\color[rgb]{0.7148,0.1953,0.1094}\boldsymbol{F}_{\textbf{\lx@text@lbrace\lx@text@rbrace}}}
elaboration is
indeed appropriate.

The first theorem states that a well-typed
{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}\boldsymbol{F}_{\textbf{{D}}}}
expression always elaborates to
a
{\color[rgb]{0.7148,0.1953,0.1094}\boldsymbol{F}_{\textbf{\lx@text@lbrace\lx@text@rbrace}}}
expression that is also well-typed in the translated context.

Theorem 5 (Type Preservation).

If
\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Sigma}}}}};\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Gamma_{C}}}}}};\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Gamma}}}}}\vdash_{tm}\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{e}}}}}:\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\sigma}}}}}\rightsquigarrow\color[rgb]{0.7148,0.1953,0.1094}{{{\color[rgb]{0.7148,0.1953,0.1094}{{e}}}}}
,

then there are unique
{\color[rgb]{0.7148,0.1953,0.1094}{{\Gamma}}}
and
{\color[rgb]{0.7148,0.1953,0.1094}{{\sigma}}}
such that
\color[rgb]{0.7148,0.1953,0.1094}{{{\color[rgb]{0.7148,0.1953,0.1094}{{\Gamma}}}}}\vdash_{tm}\color[rgb]{0.7148,0.1953,0.1094}{{{\color[rgb]{0.7148,0.1953,0.1094}{{e}}}}}:\color[rgb]{0.7148,0.1953,0.1094}{{{\color[rgb]{0.7148,0.1953,0.1094}{{\sigma}}}}}
,

where
\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Gamma_{C}}}}}};\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Gamma}}}}}\vdash_{ty}\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\sigma}}}}}\rightsquigarrow\color[rgb]{0.7148,0.1953,0.1094}{{{\color[rgb]{0.7148,0.1953,0.1094}{{\sigma}}}}}
and
\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Gamma_{C}}}}}};\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Gamma}}}}}\rightsquigarrow\color[rgb]{0.7148,0.1953,0.1094}{{{\color[rgb]{0.7148,0.1953,0.1094}{{\Gamma}}}}}
.

Secondly, and more importantly, the dynamic semantics is also preserved by the
elaboration.

Theorem 6 (Semantic Preservation).

If
\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Sigma}}}}};\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Gamma_{C}}}}}};\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\bullet}}\vdash_{tm}\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{e}}}}}:\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\sigma}}}}}\rightsquigarrow\color[rgb]{0.7148,0.1953,0.1094}{{{\color[rgb]{0.7148,0.1953,0.1094}{{e}}}}}
and
\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Sigma}}}}}\vdash\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{e}}}}}\longrightarrow^{*}\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{v}}}}}

then there exists a
{\color[rgb]{0.7148,0.1953,0.1094}{{v}}}
such that
\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Sigma}}}}};\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Gamma_{C}}}}}};\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\bullet}}\vdash_{tm}\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{v}}}}}:\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\sigma}}}}}\rightsquigarrow\color[rgb]{0.7148,0.1953,0.1094}{{{\color[rgb]{0.7148,0.1953,0.1094}{{v}}}}}
and
\color[rgb]{0.7148,0.1953,0.1094}{{{\color[rgb]{0.7148,0.1953,0.1094}{{e}}}}}\simeq\color[rgb]{0.7148,0.1953,0.1094}{{{\color[rgb]{0.7148,0.1953,0.1094}{{v}}}}}
.

Thirdly, the elaboration is entirely deterministic.

Theorem 7 (Determinism).

If
\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Sigma}}}}};\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Gamma_{C}}}}}};\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Gamma}}}}}\vdash_{tm}\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{e}}}}}:\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\sigma}}}}}\rightsquigarrow\color[rgb]{0.7148,0.1953,0.1094}{{{\color[rgb]{0.7148,0.1953,0.1094}{{e}}}_{{\mathrm{1}}}}}
and
\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Sigma}}}}};\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Gamma_{C}}}}}};\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Gamma}}}}}\vdash_{tm}\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{e}}}}}:\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\sigma}}}}}\rightsquigarrow\color[rgb]{0.7148,0.1953,0.1094}{{{\color[rgb]{0.7148,0.1953,0.1094}{{e}}}_{{\mathrm{2}}}}}
,
then
\color[rgb]{0.7148,0.1953,0.1094}{{{\color[rgb]{0.7148,0.1953,0.1094}{{e}}}_{{\mathrm{1}}}}}=\color[rgb]{0.7148,0.1953,0.1094}{{{\color[rgb]{0.7148,0.1953,0.1094}{{e}}}_{{\mathrm{2}}}}}
.

6.3.
Elaboration Decomposition

An elaboration from
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.7227}\boldsymbol{\lambda}_{\textbf{{TC}}}}
to
{\color[rgb]{0.7148,0.1953,0.1094}\boldsymbol{F}_{\textbf{\lx@text@lbrace\lx@text@rbrace}}}
can always be decomposed into two
elaborations through
{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}\boldsymbol{F}_{\textbf{{D}}}}
.
This intuition is formalized in
Theorems
8
and
9
respectively.

Theorem 8 (Elaboration Equivalence - Expressions).

If
\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.7227}{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.7227}{{P}}}}};\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.7227}{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.7227}{{\Gamma_{C}}}}}};\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.7227}{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.7227}{{\Gamma}}}}}\vdash_{tm}\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.7227}{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.7227}{{e}}}}}\Rightarrow\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.7227}{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.7227}{{\tau}}}}}{\rightsquigarrow\color[rgb]{0.7148,0.1953,0.1094}{{{\color[rgb]{0.7148,0.1953,0.1094}{{e}}}}}}
and
\vdash_{ctx}\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.7227}{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.7227}{{P}}}}};\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.7227}{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.7227}{{\Gamma_{C}}}}}};\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.7227}{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.7227}{{\Gamma}}}}}\rightsquigarrow\color[rgb]{0.7148,0.1953,0.1094}{{{\color[rgb]{0.7148,0.1953,0.1094}{{\Gamma}}}}}

then
\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.7227}{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.7227}{{P}}}}};\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.7227}{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.7227}{{\Gamma_{C}}}}}};\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.7227}{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.7227}{{\Gamma}}}}}\vdash_{tm}^{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{M}}}\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.7227}{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.7227}{{e}}}}}\Rightarrow\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.7227}{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.7227}{{\tau}}}}}{\rightsquigarrow\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{e}}}}}}
and
\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Sigma}}}}};\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Gamma_{C}}}}}};\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Gamma}}}}}\vdash_{tm}\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{e}}}}}:\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\sigma}}}}}{\rightsquigarrow\color[rgb]{0.7148,0.1953,0.1094}{{{\color[rgb]{0.7148,0.1953,0.1094}{{e}}}}}}

where
\vdash_{ctx}^{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{M}}}\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.7227}{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.7227}{{P}}}}};\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.7227}{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.7227}{{\Gamma_{C}}}}}};\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.7227}{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.7227}{{\Gamma}}}}}\rightsquigarrow\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Sigma}}}}};\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Gamma_{C}}}}}};\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Gamma}}}}}
and
\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Gamma_{C}}}}}};\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Gamma}}}}}\rightsquigarrow\color[rgb]{0.7148,0.1953,0.1094}{{{\color[rgb]{0.7148,0.1953,0.1094}{{\Gamma}}}}}
and
\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.7227}{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.7227}{{\Gamma_{C}}}}}};\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.7227}{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.7227}{{\Gamma}}}}}\vdash_{ty}^{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{M}}}\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.7227}{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.7227}{{\tau}}}}}\,{{\rightsquigarrow\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\sigma}}}}}}}
.

Theorem 9 (Elaboration Equivalence - Dictionaries).

If
\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.7227}{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.7227}{{P}}}}};\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.7227}{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.7227}{{\Gamma_{C}}}}}};\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.7227}{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.7227}{{\Gamma}}}}}\vDash\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.7227}{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.7227}{{Q}}}}}{\rightsquigarrow\color[rgb]{0.7148,0.1953,0.1094}{{{\color[rgb]{0.7148,0.1953,0.1094}{{e}}}}}}
and
\vdash_{ctx}\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.7227}{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.7227}{{P}}}}};\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.7227}{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.7227}{{\Gamma_{C}}}}}};\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.7227}{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.7227}{{\Gamma}}}}}\rightsquigarrow\color[rgb]{0.7148,0.1953,0.1094}{{{\color[rgb]{0.7148,0.1953,0.1094}{{\Gamma}}}}}

then
\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.7227}{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.7227}{{P}}}}};\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.7227}{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.7227}{{\Gamma_{C}}}}}};\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.7227}{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.7227}{{\Gamma}}}}}\vDash^{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{M}}}\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.7227}{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.7227}{{Q}}}}}{\rightsquigarrow\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{d}}}}}}
and
\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Sigma}}}}};\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Gamma_{C}}}}}};\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Gamma}}}}}\vdash_{d}\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{d}}}}}:\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{Q}}}}}{\,\rightsquigarrow\color[rgb]{0.7148,0.1953,0.1094}{{{\color[rgb]{0.7148,0.1953,0.1094}{{e}}}}}}

where
\vdash_{ctx}^{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{M}}}\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.7227}{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.7227}{{P}}}}};\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.7227}{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.7227}{{\Gamma_{C}}}}}};\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.7227}{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.7227}{{\Gamma}}}}}\rightsquigarrow\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Sigma}}}}};\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Gamma_{C}}}}}};\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Gamma}}}}}
and
\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Gamma_{C}}}}}};\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Gamma}}}}}\rightsquigarrow\color[rgb]{0.7148,0.1953,0.1094}{{{\color[rgb]{0.7148,0.1953,0.1094}{{\Gamma}}}}}
.

Theorem
8
also has a type checking mode counterpart, which
has been omitted for space reasons. The full proofs can be
found in Section
L
of the appendix.

7.
Coherence Revisited

As mentioned previously in Section
5
, the invariant that type
class instances do not overlap is crucial in proving Theorem
3
.
This uniqueness property is made explicit in
{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}\boldsymbol{F}_{\textbf{{D}}}}
.
Our proof thus proceeds by elaborating the
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.7227}\boldsymbol{\lambda}_{\textbf{{TC}}}}
expression to two possibly
different
{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}\boldsymbol{F}_{\textbf{{D}}}}
expressions and subsequently elaborating these
{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}\boldsymbol{F}_{\textbf{{D}}}}

expressions to
{\color[rgb]{0.7148,0.1953,0.1094}\boldsymbol{F}_{\textbf{\lx@text@lbrace\lx@text@rbrace}}}
expressions.
Consequently, the proof is split in two main steps.
The first part is the most involved, where we use a technique based on logical
relations to prove that any two
{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}\boldsymbol{F}_{\textbf{{D}}}}
expressions originating from the same

{\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.7227}\boldsymbol{\lambda}_{\textbf{{TC}}}}
expression are contextually equivalent.
The second part proves that the elaboration from
{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}\boldsymbol{F}_{\textbf{{D}}}}
to

{\color[rgb]{0.7148,0.1953,0.1094}\boldsymbol{F}_{\textbf{\lx@text@lbrace\lx@text@rbrace}}}
is contextual equivalence preserving. This step follows
straightforwardly from the fact that the
{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}\boldsymbol{F}_{\textbf{{D}}}}
-to-
{\color[rgb]{0.7148,0.1953,0.1094}\boldsymbol{F}_{\textbf{\lx@text@lbrace\lx@text@rbrace}}}
elaboration is deterministic.
Together, these prove that the elaboration from
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.7227}\boldsymbol{\lambda}_{\textbf{{TC}}}}
to
{\color[rgb]{0.7148,0.1953,0.1094}\boldsymbol{F}_{\textbf{\lx@text@lbrace\lx@text@rbrace}}}
through

{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}\boldsymbol{F}_{\textbf{{D}}}}
is coherent. Theorem
4
follows from this result,
together with Theorem
8
.

The remainder of this section explains the techniques we used to prove
Theorem
3
in detail.

7.1.
Coherent Elaboration from
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.7227}\boldsymbol{\lambda}_{\textbf{{TC}}}}
to
{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}\boldsymbol{F}_{\textbf{{D}}}}

7.1.1.
Logical Relations.

Logical relations
(
Plotkin 1973
;
Statman 1985
;
Tait 1967
)
are key to proving contextual equivalence. In
our type system, the logical relation for expressions is mostly standard,
though the relation for dictionaries is novel.

Dictionaries.

The logical relation over two open dictionaries is defined by means of an
auxiliary relation on closed dictionaries.
We define this value relation for closed dictionaries as follows.
Note that from now on, we will omit elaborations when they are entirely
irrelevant. The appendix uses the same convention.

Definition 0 (Value Relation for Dictionaries).

The dictionary values
\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{D}}}\,\overline{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\sigma}}}_{\mathit{j}}\,{\overline{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{dv}}}}_{{\mathrm{1}}\,\mathit{i}}}}
and
\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{D}}}\,\overline{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\sigma}}}_{\mathit{j}}\,{\overline{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{dv}}}}_{{\mathrm{2}}\,\mathit{i}}}}
are in the value relation, defined as:

\displaystyle(\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Sigma}}}_{{\mathrm{1}}}}}:\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{D}}}\,\overline{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\sigma}}}_{\mathit{j}}\,{\overline{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{dv}}}}_{{\mathrm{1}}\,\mathit{i}}}},\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Sigma}}}_{{\mathrm{2}}}}}:\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{D}}}\,\overline{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\sigma}}}_{\mathit{j}}\,{\overline{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{dv}}}}_{{\mathrm{2}}\,\mathit{i}}}})\in\mathcal{V}\llbracket\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{Q}}}}}\rrbracket^{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Gamma_{C}}}}}}}_{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{R}}}}}}\triangleq({(\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Sigma}}}_{{\mathrm{1}}}}}:\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{dv}}}_{{\mathrm{1}}\,\mathit{i}}}},\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Sigma}}}_{{\mathrm{2}}}}}:\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{dv}}}_{{\mathrm{2}}\,\mathit{i}}}})\in\mathcal{V}\llbracket\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{[\overline{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\sigma}}}_{\mathit{j}}/{\overline{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{a}}}}_{\mathit{j}}]{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{Q}}}_{\mathit{i}}}}\rrbracket^{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Gamma_{C}}}}}}}_{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{R}}}}}}}\penalty\ ,\penalty\ \forall{i})

\displaystyle\qquad\begin{aligned} &\land\,\,\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Sigma}}}_{{\mathrm{1}}}}};\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Gamma_{C}}}}}};\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\bullet}}\vdash_{d}\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{D}}}\,\overline{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\sigma}}}_{\mathit{j}}\,{\overline{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{dv}}}}_{{\mathrm{1}}\,\mathit{i}}}}:\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{R}}}({\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{Q}}})}}\,\,\land\,\,\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Sigma}}}_{{\mathrm{2}}}}};\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Gamma_{C}}}}}};\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\bullet}}\vdash_{d}\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{D}}}\,\overline{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\sigma}}}_{\mathit{j}}\,{\overline{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{dv}}}}_{{\mathrm{2}}\,\mathit{i}}}}:\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{R}}}({\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{Q}}})}},\\
&\textit{where }(\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{D}}}}}:\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\forall{\overline{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{a}}}}_{\mathit{j}}.{\overline{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{Q}}}}_{\mathit{i}}\Rightarrow{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{Q}}}^{\prime}}}).\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{m}}}}}\mapsto\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{e}}}_{{\mathrm{1}}}}}\in\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Sigma}}}_{{\mathrm{1}}}}}\land\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{Q}}}}}=\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{[\overline{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\sigma}}}_{\mathit{j}}/{\overline{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{a}}}}_{\mathit{j}}]{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{Q}}}^{\prime}}}\end{aligned}

The value relation is indexed by the dictionary type
{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{Q}}}
.
We require both dictionaries to be well-typed, and their dictionary arguments to
be in the value relation as well.
The relation has four additional parameters:
the contexts
\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Sigma}}}_{{\mathrm{1}}}}}
and
\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Sigma}}}_{{\mathrm{2}}}}}
, which annotate the dictionaries, the
class environment
{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Gamma_{C}}}}
, used in the well-typing condition,
and the type substitution
{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{R}}}
.

In order to define logical equivalence between open dictionaries, we substitute
all free variables with closed terms, thus reducing them to closed dictionary
values. Three kinds of variables exist (term variables
{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{x}}}
, type
variables
{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{a}}}
and dictionary variables
{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\delta}}}
). This results in three
separate semantic interpretations of the typing context
{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Gamma}}}
.
The type substitution
\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{R}}}}}\in\mathcal{F}\llbracket\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Gamma}}}}}\rrbracket^{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Gamma_{C}}}}}}}
maps all type variables

\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{a}}}}}\in\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Gamma}}}}}
onto closed types.

\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\phi}}}}}\in\mathcal{G}\llbracket\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Gamma}}}}}\rrbracket^{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Sigma}}}_{{\mathrm{1}}}}},\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Sigma}}}_{{\mathrm{2}}}}},\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Gamma_{C}}}}}}}_{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{R}}}}}}
maps each term
variable
\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{x}}}}}\in\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Gamma}}}}}
to two expressions
\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{e}}}_{{\mathrm{1}}}}}
and

\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{e}}}_{{\mathrm{2}}}}}
that are in the
expression value relation (see Definition
3
),
and
\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\gamma}}}}}\in\mathcal{H}\llbracket\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Gamma}}}}}\rrbracket^{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Sigma}}}_{{\mathrm{1}}}}},\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Sigma}}}_{{\mathrm{2}}}}},\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Gamma_{C}}}}}}}_{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{R}}}}}}
maps each dictionary
variable
\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\delta}}}}}\in\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Gamma}}}}}
to two logically related dictionary values.
We use
\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\phi}}}_{{\mathrm{1}}}}}
and
\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\phi}}}_{{\mathrm{2}}}}}
to denote the substitution for the first
and second expression, respectively.

Definition 0 (Logical Equivalence for Dictionaries).

Two dictionaries
\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{d}}}_{{\mathrm{1}}}}}
and
\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{d}}}_{{\mathrm{2}}}}}
are logically equivalent, defined as:

\displaystyle\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Gamma_{C}}}}}};\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Gamma}}}}}\vdash\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Sigma}}}_{{\mathrm{1}}}}}:\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{d}}}_{{\mathrm{1}}}}}\simeq_{log}\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Sigma}}}_{{\mathrm{2}}}}}:\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{d}}}_{{\mathrm{2}}}}}:\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{Q}}}}}\triangleq\,\,\forall\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{R}}}}}\in\mathcal{F}\llbracket\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Gamma}}}}}\rrbracket^{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Gamma_{C}}}}}}},\,\,\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\phi}}}}}\in\mathcal{G}\llbracket\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Gamma}}}}}\rrbracket^{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Sigma}}}_{{\mathrm{1}}}}},\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Sigma}}}_{{\mathrm{2}}}}},\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Gamma_{C}}}}}}}_{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{R}}}}}},\,\,\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\gamma}}}}}\in\mathcal{H}\llbracket\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Gamma}}}}}\rrbracket^{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Sigma}}}_{{\mathrm{1}}}}},\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Sigma}}}_{{\mathrm{2}}}}},\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Gamma_{C}}}}}}}_{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{R}}}}}}:

\displaystyle\qquad(\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Sigma}}}_{{\mathrm{1}}}}}:\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\gamma}}}_{{\mathrm{1}}}({\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\phi}}}_{{\mathrm{1}}}({\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{R}}}({\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{d}}}_{{\mathrm{1}}})))}},\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Sigma}}}_{{\mathrm{2}}}}}:\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\gamma}}}_{{\mathrm{2}}}({\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\phi}}}_{{\mathrm{2}}}({\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{R}}}({\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{d}}}_{{\mathrm{2}}})))}})\in\mathcal{V}\llbracket\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{Q}}}}}\rrbracket^{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Gamma_{C}}}}}}}_{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{R}}}}}}

Two dictionaries
\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{d}}}_{{\mathrm{1}}}}}
and
\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{d}}}_{{\mathrm{2}}}}}
are logically
equivalent if any substitution of their free variables (with related expressions
/ dictionaries) results in related dictionary values.

Expressions.

The value relation for expressions is mostly standard, with two notable
deviations. Firstly, the relation is defined over two different method
environments
\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Sigma}}}_{{\mathrm{1}}}}}
and
\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Sigma}}}_{{\mathrm{2}}}}}
.
Hence, both expressions are annotated with their respective
environment. Secondly, the dictionary abstraction case is novel.

Definition 0 (Value Relation for Expressions).

Two values
\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{v}}}_{{\mathrm{1}}}}}
and
\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{v}}}_{{\mathrm{2}}}}}
are in the value relation, defined as:

\displaystyle(\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Sigma}}}_{{\mathrm{1}}}}}:\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\mathit{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{True}}}}},\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Sigma}}}_{{\mathrm{2}}}}}:\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\mathit{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{True}}}}})\in\mathcal{V}\llbracket\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\mathit{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{Bool}}}}}\rrbracket^{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Gamma_{C}}}}}}}_{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{R}}}}}}

\displaystyle(\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Sigma}}}_{{\mathrm{1}}}}}:\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\mathit{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{False}}}}},\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Sigma}}}_{{\mathrm{2}}}}}:\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\mathit{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{False}}}}})\in\mathcal{V}\llbracket\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\mathit{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{Bool}}}}}\rrbracket^{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Gamma_{C}}}}}}}_{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{R}}}}}}

\displaystyle(\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Sigma}}}_{{\mathrm{1}}}}}:\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{v}}}_{{\mathrm{1}}}}},\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Sigma}}}_{{\mathrm{2}}}}}:\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{v}}}_{{\mathrm{2}}}}})\in\mathcal{V}\llbracket\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{a}}}}}\rrbracket^{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Gamma_{C}}}}}}}_{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{R}}}}}}\triangleq

\displaystyle\qquad(\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{a}}}}}\mapsto(\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\sigma}}}}},\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\mathit{r}}}}}}))\in\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{R}}}}}\,\,\land\,\,(\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{v}}}_{{\mathrm{1}}}}},\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{v}}}_{{\mathrm{2}}}}})\in\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\mathit{r}}}}}}\,\,\land\,\,\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Sigma}}}_{{\mathrm{1}}}}};\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Gamma_{C}}}}}};\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\bullet}}\vdash_{tm}\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{v}}}_{{\mathrm{1}}}}}:\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\sigma}}}}}\,\,\land\,\,\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Sigma}}}_{{\mathrm{2}}}}};\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Gamma_{C}}}}}};\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\bullet}}\vdash_{tm}\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{v}}}_{{\mathrm{2}}}}}:\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\sigma}}}}}

Consider the interesting case of dictionary abstraction. The relation
requires the terms to be
well-typed, and the applications for all related input dictionaries
to be in the expression relation
\mathcal{E}
. The definition of this
\mathcal{E}
relation
is as follows:

Definition 0 (Expression Relation).

Two expressions
\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{e}}}_{{\mathrm{1}}}}}
and
\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{e}}}_{{\mathrm{2}}}}}
are in the expression relation, defined as:

\displaystyle(\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Sigma}}}_{{\mathrm{1}}}}}:\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{e}}}_{{\mathrm{1}}}}},\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Sigma}}}_{{\mathrm{2}}}}}:\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{e}}}_{{\mathrm{2}}}}})\in\mathcal{E}\llbracket\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\sigma}}}}}\rrbracket^{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Gamma_{C}}}}}}}_{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{R}}}}}}\triangleq\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Sigma}}}_{{\mathrm{1}}}}};\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Gamma_{C}}}}}};\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\bullet}}\vdash_{tm}\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{e}}}_{{\mathrm{1}}}}}:\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{R}}}({\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\sigma}}})}}\,\,\land\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Sigma}}}_{{\mathrm{2}}}}};\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Gamma_{C}}}}}};\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\bullet}}\vdash_{tm}\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{e}}}_{{\mathrm{2}}}}}:\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{R}}}({\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\sigma}}})}}

\displaystyle\qquad\land\exists\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{v}}}_{{\mathrm{1}}}}},\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{v}}}_{{\mathrm{2}}}}},\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Sigma}}}_{{\mathrm{1}}}}}\vdash\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{e}}}_{{\mathrm{1}}}}}\longrightarrow^{*}\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{v}}}_{{\mathrm{1}}}}},\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Sigma}}}_{{\mathrm{2}}}}}\vdash\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{e}}}_{{\mathrm{2}}}}}\longrightarrow^{*}\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{v}}}_{{\mathrm{2}}}}},(\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Sigma}}}_{{\mathrm{1}}}}}:\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{v}}}_{{\mathrm{1}}}}},\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Sigma}}}_{{\mathrm{2}}}}}:\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{v}}}_{{\mathrm{2}}}}})\in\mathcal{V}\llbracket\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\sigma}}}}}\rrbracket^{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Gamma_{C}}}}}}}_{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{R}}}}}}

In this definition, expressions are reduced to values and those values must be
in the value relation. This is well-defined because
{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}\boldsymbol{F}_{\textbf{{D}}}}
is
strongly normalizing (Theorem
3
).

Finally, we can give the definition of logical equivalence for open expressions:

Definition 0 (Logical Equivalence for Expressions).

Two expressions
\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{e}}}_{{\mathrm{1}}}}}
and
\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{e}}}_{{\mathrm{2}}}}}
are logically equivalent, defined as:

\displaystyle\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Gamma_{C}}}}}};\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Gamma}}}}}\vdash\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Sigma}}}_{{\mathrm{1}}}}}:\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{e}}}_{{\mathrm{1}}}}}\simeq_{log}\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Sigma}}}_{{\mathrm{2}}}}}:\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{e}}}_{{\mathrm{2}}}}}:\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\sigma}}}}}\triangleq\forall\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{R}}}}}\in\mathcal{F}\llbracket\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Gamma}}}}}\rrbracket^{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Gamma_{C}}}}}}},\,\,\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\phi}}}}}\in\mathcal{G}\llbracket\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Gamma}}}}}\rrbracket^{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Sigma}}}_{{\mathrm{1}}}}},\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Sigma}}}_{{\mathrm{2}}}}},\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Gamma_{C}}}}}}}_{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{R}}}}}},\,\,\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\gamma}}}}}\in\mathcal{H}\llbracket\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Gamma}}}}}\rrbracket^{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Sigma}}}_{{\mathrm{1}}}}},\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Sigma}}}_{{\mathrm{2}}}}},\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Gamma_{C}}}}}}}_{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{R}}}}}}:

\displaystyle\qquad(\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Sigma}}}_{{\mathrm{1}}}}}:\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\gamma}}}_{{\mathrm{1}}}({\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\phi}}}_{{\mathrm{1}}}({\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{R}}}({\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{e}}}_{{\mathrm{1}}})))}},\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Sigma}}}_{{\mathrm{2}}}}}:\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\gamma}}}_{{\mathrm{2}}}({\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\phi}}}_{{\mathrm{2}}}({\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{R}}}({\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{e}}}_{{\mathrm{2}}})))}})\in\mathcal{E}\llbracket\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\sigma}}}}}\rrbracket^{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Gamma_{C}}}}}}}_{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{R}}}}}}

Definition 0 (Logical Equivalence for Contexts).

Two contexts
\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{M}}}_{{\mathrm{1}}}}}
and
\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{M}}}_{{\mathrm{2}}}}}
are logically equivalent, defined as:

\displaystyle\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Sigma}}}_{{\mathrm{1}}}}}:\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{M}}}_{{\mathrm{1}}}}}\simeq_{log}\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Sigma}}}_{{\mathrm{2}}}}}:\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{M}}}_{{\mathrm{2}}}}}:(\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Gamma_{C}}}}}};\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Gamma}}}}}\Rightarrow\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\sigma}}}}})\mapsto(\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Gamma_{C}}}}}};\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Gamma}}}^{\prime}}}\Rightarrow\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\sigma}}}^{\prime}}})\triangleq

\displaystyle\qquad\forall\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{e}}}_{{\mathrm{1}}}}},\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{e}}}_{{\mathrm{2}}}}}:\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Gamma_{C}}}}}};\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Gamma}}}}}\vdash\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Sigma}}}_{{\mathrm{1}}}}}:\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{e}}}_{{\mathrm{1}}}}}\simeq_{log}\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Sigma}}}_{{\mathrm{2}}}}}:\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{e}}}_{{\mathrm{2}}}}}:\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\sigma}}}}}\,\,\Rightarrow\,\,\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Gamma_{C}}}}}};\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Gamma}}}^{\prime}}}\vdash\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Sigma}}}_{{\mathrm{1}}}}}:\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{M}}}_{{\mathrm{1}}}[{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{e}}}_{{\mathrm{1}}}]}}\simeq_{log}\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Sigma}}}_{{\mathrm{2}}}}}:\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{M}}}_{{\mathrm{2}}}[{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{e}}}_{{\mathrm{2}}}]}}:\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\sigma}}}^{\prime}}}

Design Principle of
{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}\boldsymbol{F}_{\textbf{{D}}}}

We emphasize that

Theorem 7 (Value Relation for Dictionary Values).

If
\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Sigma}}}_{{\mathrm{1}}}}};\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Gamma_{C}}}}}};\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\bullet}}\vdash_{d}\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{dv}}}_{{\mathrm{1}}}}}:\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{Q}}}}}
and
\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Sigma}}}_{{\mathrm{2}}}}};\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Gamma_{C}}}}}};\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\bullet}}\vdash_{d}\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{dv}}}_{{\mathrm{2}}}}}:\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{Q}}}}}
and
\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Gamma_{C}}}}}}\vdash\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Sigma}}}_{{\mathrm{1}}}}}\simeq_{log}\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Sigma}}}_{{\mathrm{2}}}}}

then
(\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Sigma}}}_{{\mathrm{1}}}}}:\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{dv}}}_{{\mathrm{1}}}}},\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Sigma}}}_{{\mathrm{2}}}}}:\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{dv}}}_{{\mathrm{2}}}}})\in\mathcal{V}\llbracket\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{Q}}}}}\rrbracket^{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Gamma_{C}}}}}}}_{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\bullet}}}
.

Note that two environments
\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Sigma}}}_{{\mathrm{1}}}}}

Coherent Resolution.

We now prove that constraint resolution is semantically
coherent, that is, if multiple resolutions of the same
constraint exist, they are logically equivalent.

Theorem 8 (Logical Coherence of Dictionary Resolution).

If
\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.7227}{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.7227}{{P}}}}};\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.7227}{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.7227}{{\Gamma_{C}}}}}};\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.7227}{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.7227}{{\Gamma}}}}}\vDash^{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{M}}}\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.7227}{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.7227}{{Q}}}}}{\rightsquigarrow\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{d}}}_{{\mathrm{1}}}}}}
and
\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.7227}{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.7227}{{P}}}}};\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.7227}{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.7227}{{\Gamma_{C}}}}}};\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.7227}{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.7227}{{\Gamma}}}}}\vDash^{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{M}}}\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.7227}{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.7227}{{Q}}}}}{\rightsquigarrow\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{d}}}_{{\mathrm{2}}}}}}

and
\vdash_{ctx}^{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{M}}}\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.7227}{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.7227}{{P}}}}};\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.7227}{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.7227}{{\Gamma_{C}}}}}};\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.7227}{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.7227}{{\Gamma}}}}}\rightsquigarrow\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Sigma}}}_{{\mathrm{1}}}}};\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Gamma_{C}}}}}};\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Gamma}}}}}
and
\vdash_{ctx}^{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{M}}}\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.7227}{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.7227}{{P}}}}};\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.7227}{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.7227}{{\Gamma_{C}}}}}};\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.7227}{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.7227}{{\Gamma}}}}}\rightsquigarrow\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Sigma}}}_{{\mathrm{2}}}}};\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Gamma_{C}}}}}};\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Gamma}}}}}

then
\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Gamma_{C}}}}}};\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Gamma}}}}}\vdash\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Sigma}}}_{{\mathrm{1}}}}}:\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{d}}}_{{\mathrm{1}}}}}\simeq_{log}\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{\Sigma}}}_{{\mathrm{2}}}}}:\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{d}}}_{{\mathrm{2}}}}}:\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{Q}}}}}
where
\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.7227}{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.7227}{{\Gamma_{C}}}}}};\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.7227}{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.7227}{{\Gamma}}}}}\vdash_{\mathit{Q}}^{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{M}}}\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.7227}{{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4297,0.7227}{{Q}}}}}\rightsquigarrow\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}{{Q}}}}}

Definition 0 (Contextual Equivalence for
{\color[rgb]{0.2344,0.5,0.1914}\boldsymbol{F}_{\textbf{{D}}}}
